paragraphs.en: Communities throughout New England have been attempting to regulate short-term rentals since sites like Airbnb took off in the 2010s. Now, with record-high home prices and historically low inventory, there's an increased urgency in such regulation, particularly among those who worry that developers will come in and buy up swaths of housing to flip for a fortune on the short-term rental market.
paragraphs.zh: 自爱彼迎等网站在2010年代迅速兴起以来，新英格兰各地的社区就一直在尝试监管短期出租。如今，房价创下新高，房源供应量降至历史低位，这类监管显得更加迫切。那些担心开发商会涌入、大批买下住房，再将其转为短租房以赚取巨额利润的人，尤其如此。

paragraphs.en: In New Hampshire, where the rental vacancy rate has dropped below 1 percent, housing advocates fear unchecked short-term rentals will put further pressure on an already strained market. The state Legislature recently voted against a bill that would've made it illegal for towns to create legislation restricting short-term rentals.
paragraphs.zh: 在新罕布什尔州，出租住房空置率已降至1%以下，住房权益倡导者担心，放任短期出租不受约束，会进一步加剧本就紧张的市场压力。州议会最近投票否决了一项法案；该法案原本会使各城镇制定限制短租的法规成为违法行为。

paragraphs.en: "We are at a crisis level on the supply of rental housing, " said Nick Taylor, executive director of the Workforce Housing Coalition of the Greater Seacoast. Without enough affordable housing in southern New Hampshire towns, "employers are having a hard time attracting employees, and workers are having a hard time finding a place to live, " Taylor said.
paragraphs.zh: “我们在出租住房供应方面已经到了危机的程度，”大海岸地区劳动力住房联盟执行主任尼克·泰勒说。他表示，由于新罕布什尔州南部各城镇缺少足够的可负担住房，“雇主很难吸引员工，劳动者也很难找到住处”。

paragraphs.en: However, short-term rentals also provide housing for tourists, pointed out Ryan Castle, CEO of a local association of realtor. "A lot of workers are servicing the tourist industry, and the tourism industry is serviced by those people coming in short term, " Castle said, "and so it's a cyclical effect. "
paragraphs.zh: 不过，当地一家房地产经纪人协会的首席执行官瑞安·卡斯尔指出，短租房也为游客提供了住宿。卡斯尔说：“许多劳动者为旅游业提供服务，而旅游业又靠这些短期到访的人支撑，所以这是一个循环作用。”

paragraphs.en: Short-term rentals themselves are not the crux of the issue, said Keren Hom, an expert on affordable housing policy. "I think individuals being able to rent out their second home is a good thing. If it's their vacation home anyway, and it's just empty, why can't you make money off it?" Hom said. Issues arise, however, when developers attempt to create large-scale short-term rental facilities—de facto hotels—to bypass taxes and regulations. " I think the question is, shouldn't a developer who's really building a hotel, but disguising it as not a hotel, be treated and taxed and regulated like a hotel?" Hom said.
paragraphs.zh: 可负担住房政策专家凯伦·霍恩表示，短期出租本身并不是问题的症结。她说：“我认为，个人能够把自己的第二套住房出租是件好事。如果它本来就是度假屋，而且只是空在那里，为什么不能靠它挣钱呢？”然而，当开发商试图建设大规模短租设施，也就是事实上的酒店，以规避税费和监管时，问题就出现了。霍恩说：“我认为，问题在于，一个实际上在建酒店、却把它伪装成非酒店项目的开发商，难道不应该像酒店一样被对待、征税和监管吗？”

paragraphs.en: At the end of 2018, Governor Charlie Baker of Massachusetts signed a bill to rein in those potential investor-buyers. The bill requires every rental host to register with the state, mandates they carry insurance, and opens the potential for local taxes on top of a new state levy. Boston took things even further, requiring renters to register with the city's Inspectional Services Department.
paragraphs.zh: 2018年底，马萨诸塞州州长查理·贝克签署了一项法案，以约束那些可能购入住房的投资者。该法案要求每一位出租房东向州政府登记，强制他们购买保险，并允许地方政府在新增的州税之外征收地方税。波士顿采取了更进一步的措施，要求出租者到市检查服务部门登记。

paragraphs.en: Hom said similar registration requirements could benefit struggling cities and towns, but "if we want to make a change in the housing market, the main one is we have to build a lot more. "
paragraphs.zh: 霍恩说，类似的登记要求可能有利于那些陷入困境的城镇，但“如果我们想改变住房市场，最主要的一点是，我们必须大幅增加住房建设”。
